From 4fc87c240b8f30e22b7ebaae29d57105589e1c0b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 23:28:20 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] rust_binder: fix oneway spam detection

The spam detection logic in TreeRange was executed before the current
request was inserted into the tree. So the new request was not being
factored in the spam calculation. Fix this by moving the logic after
the new range has been inserted.

Also, the detection logic for ArrayRange was missing altogether which
meant large spamming transactions could get away without being detected.
Fix this by implementing an equivalent low_oneway_space() in ArrayRange.

Note that I looked into centralizing this logic in RangeAllocator but
iterating through 'state' and 'size' got a bit too complicated (for me)
and I abandoned this effort.

Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Cc: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Fixes: eafedbc7c050 ("rust_binder: add Rust Binder driver")
Signed-off-by: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260210232949.3770644-1-cmllamas@google.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/tree.rs b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/tree.rs
index 838fdd2b47ea..48796fcdb362 100644
--- a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/tree.rs
+++ b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/tree.rs
@@ -164,15 +164,6 @@ pub(crate) fn reserve_new(
             self.free_oneway_space
         };
 
-        // Start detecting spammers once we have less than 20%
-        // of async space left (which is less than 10% of total
-        // buffer size).
-        //
-        // (This will short-circut, so `low_oneway_space` is
-        // only called when necessary.)
-        let oneway_spam_detected =
-            is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid);
-
         let (found_size, found_off, tree_node, free_tree_node) = match self.find_best_match(size) {
             None => {
                 pr_warn!("ENOSPC from range_alloc.reserve_new - size: {}", size);
@@ -203,6 +194,15 @@ pub(crate) fn reserve_new(
             self.free_tree.insert(free_tree_node);
         }
 
+        // Start detecting spammers once we have less than 20%
+        // of async space left (which is less than 10% of total
+        // buffer size).
+        //
+        // (This will short-circuit, so `low_oneway_space` is
+        // only called when necessary.)
+        let oneway_spam_detected =
+            is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid);
+
         Ok((found_off, oneway_spam_detected))
     }
 
--

diff --git a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/mod.rs b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/mod.rs
index 2301e2bc1a1f..1f4734468ff1 100644
--- a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/mod.rs
+++ b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/mod.rs
@@ -188,11 +188,11 @@ pub(crate) fn reserve_new(&mut self, mut args: ReserveNewArgs<T>) -> Result<Rese
                 self.reserve_new(args)
             }
             Impl::Array(array) => {
-                let offset =
+                let (offset, oneway_spam_detected) =
                     array.reserve_new(args.debug_id, args.size, args.is_oneway, args.pid)?;
                 Ok(ReserveNew::Success(ReserveNewSuccess {
                     offset,
-                    oneway_spam_detected: false,
+                    oneway_spam_detected,
                     _empty_array_alloc: args.empty_array_alloc,
                     _new_tree_alloc: args.new_tree_alloc,
                     _tree_alloc: args.tree_alloc,

diff --git a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/array.rs b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/array.rs
index 07e1dec2ce63..ada1d1b4302e 100644
--- a/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/array.rs
+++ b/drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/array.rs
@@ -118,7 +118,7 @@ pub(crate) fn reserve_new(
         size: usize,
         is_oneway: bool,
         pid: Pid,
-    ) -> Result<usize> {
+    ) -> Result<(usize, bool)> {
         // Compute new value of free_oneway_space, which is set only on success.
         let new_oneway_space = if is_oneway {
             match self.free_oneway_space.checked_sub(size) {
@@ -146,7 +146,38 @@ pub(crate) fn reserve_new(
             .ok()
             .unwrap();
 
-        Ok(insert_at_offset)
+        // Start detecting spammers once we have less than 20%
+        // of async space left (which is less than 10% of total
+        // buffer size).
+        //
+        // (This will short-circuit, so `low_oneway_space` is
+        // only called when necessary.)
+        let oneway_spam_detected =
+            is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid);
+
+        Ok((insert_at_offset, oneway_spam_detected))
+    }
+
+    /// Find the amount and size of buffers allocated by the current caller.
+    ///
+    /// The idea is that once we cross the threshold, whoever is responsible
+    /// for the low async space is likely to try to send another async transaction,
+    /// and at some point we'll catch them in the act.  This is more efficient
+    /// than keeping a map per pid.
+    fn low_oneway_space(&self, calling_pid: Pid) -> bool {
+        let mut total_alloc_size = 0;
+        let mut num_buffers = 0;
+
+        // Warn if this pid has more than 50 transactions, or more than 50% of
+        // async space (which is 25% of total buffer size). Oneway spam is only
+        // detected when the threshold is exceeded.
+        for range in &self.ranges {
+            if range.state.is_oneway() && range.state.pid() == calling_pid {
+                total_alloc_size += range.size;
+                num_buffers += 1;
+            }
+        }
+        num_buffers > 50 || total_alloc_size > self.size / 4
     }
 
     pub(crate) fn reservation_abort(&mut self, offset: usize) -> Result<FreedRange> {

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes two bugs in the oneway spam detection logic of the Rust Binder driver's range allocator:

### 1. `tree.rs` – Reorder spam detection
- **Modification**: Moved the oneway spam detection check from *before* the new range insertion to *after* it.
- **Rationale**: Previously, the detection ran before the current request was added to the tree, so the new transaction was not accounted for in the spam calculation. Moving it after insertion ensures the new request's contribution is included in `low_oneway_space()`.

### 2. `array.rs` – Add missing spam detection
- **Modification**:
  - Added a new `low_oneway_space()` method for `ArrayRange`, analogous to the one in `TreeRange`. It counts how many oneway buffers the calling PID has allocated (by iterating through `ranges`) and returns `true` if the PID has more than 50 buffers or its total allocated size exceeds 25% of the total buffer size.
  - Updated the `reserve_new()` method of `ArrayRange` to compute the spam flag after inserting the new range, similarly to the corrected logic in `tree.rs`.
  - Changed the return type of `reserve_new()` from `Result<usize>` to `Result<(usize, bool)>` to pass back the spam detection result.
- **Rationale**: The original `ArrayRange` implementation completely lacked oneway spam detection, allowing large spamming transactions to go undetected. This patch fills that gap.

### 3. `mod.rs` – Propagate spam detection from `ArrayRange`
- **Modification**: Updated the `Array` branch in `reserve_new()` to unpack the new tuple `(offset, oneway_spam_detected)` from `array.reserve_new()` and pass it into the `ReserveNewSuccess` result, instead of always hardcoding `false`.
- **Rationale**: This is a minimal plumbing change to propagate the newly computed spam flag from the array implementation up to the caller, matching the existing behavior of the tree implementation.

### Relationships
- The fix in `tree.rs` alone would not have helped the array implementation; a separate implementation of `low_oneway_space()` and the spam check was needed in `array.rs`.
- The change in `mod.rs` is a direct consequence of adding spam detection to `ArrayRange`: without it, the detection result would be lost.
- All three changes together ensure that both `TreeRange` and `ArrayRange` perform oneway spam detection correctly (after insertion) and report the result consistently.

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications per File

1. **`drivers/android/binder/range_alloc/mod.rs`**  
   - In `reserve_new()`, the call to `array.reserve_new()` now returns a tuple `(offset, oneway_spam_detected)` instead of just `offset`.

- **Tree spam timing fix**: The move in `tree.rs` ensures that when `low_oneway_space()` iterates over the tree, the current request’s allocation (just inserted) is included. Prior to the patch, it was evaluated before insertion, so the request was missed, making the detection less accurate.  
- **Array spam detection addition**: The changes in `array.rs` (added detection logic) and `mod.rs` (propagating the result) together fill a gap: the previous code completely skipped spam detection for `ArrayRange`, allowing large oneway transactions to bypass the spam check.  
- **Consistency**: The spam detection algorithm (threshold: free space < 10% of total size, then check PID’s usage) is now implemented identically for both `TreeRange` and `ArrayRange`, differing only in the internal data structure used for iteration (tree nodes vs. a list of ranges).

## Summary of Modifications

This patch fixes two issues in the oneway spam detection logic of the Rust Binder driver, affecting both `TreeRange` and `ArrayRange` allocation strategies.

### 1. `tree.rs` – Fix timing of spam detection in `TreeRange::reserve_new`
- **Before:** The spam detection check (`low_oneway_space`) was performed *before* the new request was inserted into the tree. This meant the new allocation was not counted in the spam calculation, weakening detection.
- **After:** The check is moved to *after* the new range has been successfully inserted into the free and used trees. This ensures the new request’s size is factored into the free space calculation and the subsequent spam detection runs against the updated state.

### 2. `array.rs` – Implement spam detection in `ArrayRange::reserve_new`
- **Before:** The `ArrayRange` version of `reserve_new` returned only the offset and did not perform any oneway spam detection. Consequently, large spamming transactions using array-based allocation could evade detection.
- **After:** 
  - The return type of `reserve_new` is changed from `Result<usize>` to `Result<(usize, bool)>` so it can return a spam detection flag.
  - A new method `low_oneway_space` is added, which iterates over the allocated ranges to sum the total size and count of buffers owned by the calling PID (only for oneway transactions). If the count exceeds 50 or the total allocated size exceeds 25% of total buffer space, spam is detected.

- **Before:** When using the `Array` implementation, `oneway_spam_detected` was hardcoded to `false`.

- The `tree.rs` change fixes a bug where the new request was not counted in the spam detection for the tree-based allocator.
- The `array.rs` change adds the missing spam detection for the array-based allocator, using the same heuristic as `tree.rs`.
- The `mod.rs` change updates the glue code to properly forward the detection result from the array allocator, ensuring both allocators provide consistent spam detection behavior to higher layers. Together, these changes ensure that oneway spam detection is correctly applied in both allocation paths.
